paper.title: Identification and Estimation of Local Average Treatment Effects

paper_reference.paper_question: 在二元工具变量、二元参与和二元结果下，仅工具变量有效能否识别有意义的平均处理效应？需要什么额外条件？
paper_reference.target: 遵从者的局部平均处理效应 LATE：E[Y_i(1)-Y_i(0) | D_i(1) != D_i(0)]。
paper_reference.source_location: Imbens & Angrist (1994), Econometrica 62(2):467-475, Conditions 1-2 and Theorem 1, pp. 468-470.
paper_reference.formula: LATE = (E[Y|Z=1]-E[Y|Z=0]) / (E[D|Z=1]-E[D|Z=0]), with a nonzero positive denominator. For general z,w: alpha_{z,w} = (E[Y|Z=z]-E[Y|Z=w]) / (P(z)-P(w)), P(z)=E[D|Z=z].
conditions: Condition 1: (Y_i(0),Y_i(1),D_i(w)) is jointly independent of Z_i for every w; P(w)=E[D_i|Z_i=w] is a nontrivial function of w.
Condition 2 (monotonicity): for all z,w, either D_i(z)>=D_i(w) for all i or D_i(z)<=D_i(w) for all i; no defiers.
Positive compliance: the denominator P(z)-P(w) is nonzero and positive for the chosen direction.
Finite conditional expectations for the outcomes used in the ratio.

sample_analog.note: This is a sample analog for checking the formula and sign. It is not the paper's data and not a population LATE.

what_paper_supports: Condition 1 alone is not sufficient to identify an average treatment effect.
Conditions 1 and 2 identify LATE for compliers.
LATE is not the population ATE.
The IV estimand is a weighted average of LATEs when the instrument has multiple values.
what_paper_does_not_support: It does not identify ATE for the whole population.
It does not justify LATE without monotonicity.
It does not support network IV, continuous instruments, weak-instrument inference, or 2SLS extensions.
It does not show that the current software has an IV backend.

available_information_a4.population: No population joint law or population conditional means are provided; the table is a finite sample.
available_information_a4.instrument: Binary eligibility Z, randomized with probability 1/2.

not_adopted: No assumption that LATE equals ATE.
No assumption that the finite sample is the population.

original.reason: The current repository has no registered IV reader or IV mathematical backend. The paper's LATE formula is a paper reference, not a current software capability.

missing_condition.reason: The paper's LATE is not identified without monotonicity; the software has no IV backend either. The system should not return a LATE number.

changed_target.reason: The paper identifies LATE, not the population ATE. ATE bounds require separate literature (e.g., Balke-Pearl 1997) and a separate implementation; current software has no IV backend.

actual_run.note: No IV business run was attempted because there is no IV reader/backend. This is an honest UNSUPPORTED, not a proof of non-identification.

notes: Software expectation is UNSUPPORTED for all three variants. The paper reference is recorded separately and is not turned into a software result.
